objectives: Classify dehydration using IMNCI signs before prescribing medicines.
Calculate and start ORS Plan B correctly for a 10 kg child.
Provide zinc and caregiver counseling with a 4-hour reassessment plan.
takeaways: Restlessness, sunken eyes, eager drinking, and slow skin pinch indicate some dehydration.
Plan B for 10 kg child is 75 ml/kg over 4 hours (750 ml total).
Zinc 20 mg daily for 10-14 days should be paired with feeding and return advice.
learnCaseOverrides.blurb: An 18-month-old with watery diarrhoea needs rapid dehydration classification and practical ORS planning.

sections.title: Caregiver report
sections.text: Mother says stool is frequent and child drinks quickly but remains thirsty.

coach.title: Brian looks irritable and thirsty
coach.body: Your first task is dehydration classification, not automatic medicine selection.

sections.title: Hydration signs
sections.text: Restless/irritable, sunken eyes, drinks eagerly, skin pinch returns slowly.
sections.emphasis: No lethargy and not unable to drink.

coach.title: Which dehydration class fits best?
coach.body: Use signs exactly as IMNCI describes.

question.prompt: How should this child be classified?
question.right: Correct. These signs support some dehydration, not severe dehydration, because the child is not lethargic and can drink.
question.wrong: The sign pattern matches some dehydration. Severe dehydration requires more dangerous findings like lethargy/unconsciousness or inability to drink.

sections.title: Rehydration plan
sections.detail: 75 ml/kg over 4 hours = 750 ml for 10 kg child

coach.title: Choose the correct immediate treatment
coach.body: Avoid common arithmetic and dosing mistakes.

question.prompt: What is the best next action?

options.text: Start ORS 750 ml over 4 hours and give zinc 20 mg daily for 10-14 days
Give antidiarrhoeal syrup only, no ORS required
Give IV fluids immediately to all diarrhoea cases
Send home first, then start ORS only if still sick tomorrow

question.right: Correct. For some dehydration at 10 kg, Plan B is 750 ml ORS over 4 hours plus zinc 20 mg daily.
question.wrong: This child already has dehydration signs. Delaying ORS or using non-IMNCI shortcuts risks progression to severe dehydration.

coach.title: What counseling should accompany treatment?
coach.body: Counseling is part of the intervention, not optional.

options.text: Teach ORS mixing/use, continue feeding, give zinc daily, and explain danger signs
Stop feeds until diarrhoea fully resolves
Avoid ORS at home to prevent overhydration
Use antibiotics first for all watery diarrhoea

question.right: Correct. Continued fluids/feeding and clear return precautions prevent deterioration after discharge.
question.wrong: Stopping feeds or avoiding home ORS worsens recovery. IMNCI emphasizes caregiver-led oral rehydration and danger-sign recognition.

sections.title: Case outcome
sections.text: You classified some dehydration correctly and initiated Plan B with zinc and caregiver teaching.
sections.emphasis: Classification before treatment prevented both under- and over-treatment.

coach.title: Key teaching points
coach.body: In IMNCI diarrhoea care, the hydration signs drive treatment. Brian's exam matched some dehydration, so ORS Plan B and zinc with reassessment was the right HC III plan.
